user.title: Set up Mikrotik Router
user.description: Set up Mikrotik Router integration. SSL with certificate verification is recommended; turn them off only if the router has no api-ssl service or no trusted certificate.

data_description.allowed_changes: Untick a kind of change to remove its switches or buttons and refuse it at the RouterOS API. Untick everything for read-only monitoring.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Mikrotik Router
reconfigure.description: Update the connection settings. Leave the password blank to keep the current password.

error.cannot_identify: The router identity could not be verified. Ensure the RouterOS user can read System > License.
error.librouteros_api_mismatch: Incompatible librouteros API; update this integration.

abort.wrong_router: The connection settings belong to a different router.

insecure_connection.title: {name} uses an unencrypted RouterOS connection
insecure_connection.description: The {name} entry logs in to RouterOS over the plain API (port 8728), so the password and all data cross the network unencrypted. Enable the api-ssl service on the router, then reconfigure the entry with SSL and certificate verification on.

unverified_connection.title: {name} does not verify the router certificate
unverified_connection.description: The {name} entry uses SSL without verifying the router certificate, so an attacker on the network could impersonate the router and capture the password. Install a certificate on the router that matches the configured host and is trusted by Home Assistant, then reconfigure the entry with certificate verification on.

entry_not_found.message: The RouterOS entry {entry} could not be found. Refresh the integration and try again.

managed_by_capsman.message: {entity} is managed by CAPsMAN and cannot be controlled directly.

missing_permissions.message: The RouterOS user is missing the required permissions: {permissions}.

routeros_command_failed.message: The router did not complete the requested action. Check the connection and RouterOS permissions.

change_not_allowed.message: Home Assistant isn't allowed to make this change ({action}) on the router. Tick it in the Allowed router changes option to allow it.

data.track_iface_clients: Show client MAC and IP on interfaces

data_description.allowed_changes: Switches for a kind of change that isn't allowed are removed and shown as binary sensors instead; buttons need scripts, and installing updates needs firmware updates. Writes that aren't allowed are refused at the RouterOS API. Untick everything for read-only.
